boundary_rationale: Onset at 5:9: behind the seam, 5:8 ends the leaven image; across it, rp:1Cor.5.9 (Ἔγραψα ὑμῖν ἐν τῇ ἐπιστολῇ) introduces the earlier letter. RP pilcrow at 5:9 coincides with this onset (EXTRACTED) and informs without deciding. Inside the span, rp:1Cor.5.11 (Νῦν δὲ ἔγραψα ὑμῖν) restates the instruction and 5:12 asks a question on judging outsiders. Close at 5:13/6:1: the unit ends on a citation-imperative, rp:1Cor.5.13 (Καὶ ἐξαρεῖτε τὸν πονηρὸν ἐξ ὑμῶν αὐτῶν), and the next verse opens a new complaint about lawsuits, rp:1Cor.6.1 (Τολμᾷ τις ὑμῶν), at the parent seam.

strongest_rejected_alternative: A seam at 5:11/5:12, opening a short unit on judging outsiders with the ti gar question, rp:1Cor.5.12 (Τί γάρ μοι). Declined because 5:12-5:13 answer the clarification of 5:9-5:11 (whom the assembly judges) and lead straight into the expulsion imperative; split there, the closing imperative would lose its premise.

device_notes: The closing imperative differs between witnesses: RP has a future, rp:1Cor.5.13 (Καὶ ἐξαρεῖτε τὸν πονηρὸν), and SBL reads an imperative, sbl:1Cor.5.13 (⸀ἐξάρατε τὸν πονηρὸν), with a critical sign at that word. The close does not depend on the mood. Divided reading, REPORTED: the discipline of 5:1-5:13 is read by some as permanent exclusion and by others as remedial; the seam stands under both. The vice-list wording of 5:10-5:11 recurs in 6:9-6:10 (INFERRED link, also disclosed on 6:9-6:11). device_notes: A two-verse unit, kept as a complete move. SBLGNT words the opening of 7:39 differently, without the dative noun that follows the verb in RP (sbl:1Cor.7.39); the onset does not rest on it. The close at 7:40/8:1 is argued on content: Paul's own judgment ends the widow clause at 7:40, and the peri de topic formula at 8:1 opens the next matter at the parent seam.
